decisions.reason: The question identifies the near-real-time tracking goal and the one-year lag. The method mentions monthly global grids, but the question does not connect those geographically resolved estimates to tracking recent changes.

The poster gives the correct counts and names Global Carbon Budget 2022. It omits that the benchmarks are monthly surface ocean fCO2 outputs available through December 2021 and that the eight data products are observation-based.

The poster names convolutional neural networks and semi-supervised learning. It omits the nonlinear relationship learned for each benchmark and the combination of supervised prediction error with a consistency loss between weakly and strongly feature-masked inputs.
The poster gives the monthly global coverage, both variables, and the correct date range. It omits the 1° × 1° resolution and the availability of estimates for each of the 18 benchmarks.
The finding uses µatm for an fCO2 discrepancy. The poster omits the flux density unit, the inputs to the bulk flux calculation, and the meaning of positive flux.

The finding gives the 2020–2021 comparison years and refers to original outputs. It omits the 2000–2019 training period, the held-out status of 2020–2021, and the comparison against each benchmark's original outputs for the same months.
The poster reports close spatial agreement for group averages. It omits the fCO2 correlation analysis result that most benchmark comparisons had R² above 0.9.

The poster reports a spatial discrepancy threshold. It omits the reproduced seasonality of both benchmark groups, the generally slightly higher global monthly means, and the finding that most of those differences were below 3 µatm.
The poster omits the difficulty of predicting extremes, the larger errors in the equatorial Pacific and Arctic, and the impact of historical Arctic data gaps on MPI-SOMFFN accuracy.

notes: The under-10 µatm statement concerns spatial discrepancies in group averages, so the missing under-3 µatm global monthly mean result is a coverage deduction. The caption identifies the figure as the 10-model average, while the finding also discusses the eight data products. The supplied image and text show no contradiction between the figure and caption. Section headings are easy to scan, but the figure's month labels, axes, and legend are small, and fCO2 and GOBMs appear in the finding without explicit definitions. The prominent finding competes with the question as the first section to read, though the caption is easy to associate with the figure. This is an AI review of the supplied materials.
